name: cardigan-eisteddfod-1176
description: A Welsh prince invited poets and musicians to compete at his newly built castle, the first recorded gathering of its kind.

name: liszt-lisztomania-berlin
description: Hungarian piano virtuoso Franz Liszt's Berlin recitals drew swooning, souvenir-hunting crowds, a frenzy later named after him.

name: jenny-lind-america-tour
description: The Swedish soprano, promoted by P.T. Barnum, sang to packed halls across the United States on a hugely hyped tour.

name: carnegie-hall-opens
description: Tchaikovsky guest-conducted at the opening of Andrew Carnegie's New York concert hall, which became a world-famous stage.

name: first-promenade-concert
description: Henry Wood conducted the first season of cheap, informal orchestral concerts at London's Queen's Hall, the start of the Proms.

name: mahler-symphony-of-a-thousand
description: Gustav Mahler conducted his Eighth Symphony in Munich with vast choirs and orchestra, the largest-scale premiere of his career.

name: hollywood-bowl-first-season
description: A natural hillside amphitheatre in Los Angeles hosted its first summer concerts under the stars, becoming a landmark venue.

name: benny-goodman-carnegie-hall
description: The King of Swing led his band and Black jazz stars on the stage of a classical temple, a landmark moment for jazz.

name: marian-anderson-lincoln-memorial
description: Barred from a Washington concert hall, the contralto sang outdoors before a huge crowd, a landmark in the civil rights struggle.

name: moondog-coronation-ball
description: Cleveland radio host Alan Freed's rhythm and blues dance in a packed arena is often called the first rock and roll concert.

name: first-newport-jazz-festival
description: A Rhode Island seaside town hosted the first of an annual jazz festival that became a model for outdoor music gatherings.

name: first-glastonbury-festival
description: A Somerset dairy farmer hosted a small, cheap music gathering that grew into Britain's most famous summer festival.

name: the-band-last-waltz
description: The Band's farewell concert in San Francisco, with guests including Dylan and Clapton, was filmed by Martin Scorsese.

name: simon-garfunkel-central-park
description: The folk duo reunited for a free concert on New York's Great Lawn that drew hundreds of thousands of fans.

name: three-tenors-rome
description: Pavarotti, Domingo and Carreras sang together in the ancient Baths of Caracalla on the eve of a football final.

name: freddie-mercury-tribute-concert
description: Stars joined Queen's surviving members at Wembley Stadium to honour their late singer and raise money against AIDS.

name: first-coachella-festival
description: A two-day music festival in a California desert polo field launched what became one of the world's biggest annual festivals.

name: concert-for-new-york-city
description: Paul McCartney, The Who and others played Madison Square Garden to honour firefighters and police after the terror attacks.

name: live-8-concerts
description: Concerts in several G8 countries urged world leaders to cancel African debt and boost aid, echoing an earlier famous benefit show.

name: tupac-hologram-coachella
description: A projected digital likeness of the late rapper performed alongside Dr. Dre and Snoop Dogg before a festival crowd.

name: beychella-coachella
description: Beyonce became the first Black woman to headline a major desert festival, with a marching-band spectacle that was widely hailed.

name: one-world-together-at-home
description: Stars performed from their living rooms in a livestreamed charity broadcast during lockdowns, raising money for health workers.

name: taylor-swift-eras-tour-begins
description: A stadium tour spanning all the pop star's album periods opened in Arizona and became the highest-grossing concert tour ever.
